We need to generate new test cases for get(String) method, avoiding duplication with existing cases. Existing cases cover:

- missingKey: key not in collectorMap, returns null.
- plainObject: key in collectorMap with non-Collector, returns that value.
- collectorOnly: key maps to Collector, collectorLoadMap does not have value (null), returns collector instance.
- collectorWithLoad: key maps to Collector, collectorLoadMap has non-null, returns loaded value.
- loadOnly: collectorLoadMap has value but collectorMap missing, returns null.

We need other scenarios: maybe collectorLoadMap has null value explicitly, collectorMap has null value, both maps have null, key maps to Collector but collectorLoadMap has null value (should return collector). Also test when collectorMap contains null (explicitly stored) and collectorLoadMap maybe has non-null? The code: object = collectorMap.get(name); if (object instanceof Collector<?> && collectorLoadMap.get(name) != null) return collectorLoadMap.get(name); return collectorMap.get(name);

So if collectorMap contains null, object is null, instanceof fails, returns collectorMap.get(name) which is null. So test that.

Also test that collectorLoadMap contains value but collectorMap has a non-Collector (e.g., plain object) - should return plain object, ignoring load map. Already similar to plainObject but not with load map present. So add case where both maps have entries but collectorMap value is non-Collector, collectorLoadMap has non-null. Expect plain object.

Also test that collectorMap has Collector, collectorLoadMap has null (explicit null). Should return collector.

Also test that collectorMap has Collector, collectorLoadMap has value but that value is null (explicitly null). Since condition checks collectorLoadMap.get(name) != null, fails, returns collectorMap.get(name) (collector). So same as null case.

Also test that collectorMap has Collector subclass (maybe a custom Collector implementation) and load map has value; ensure returns loaded value.

Edge cases: name is null -> Map.get(null) returns null (no NPE). So get(null) should return null. Also name empty string.

Potential concurrency? Not needed.

Thus produce new test cases: 

1. "nullKeyInMaps": name null, both maps empty, expect null.

2. "emptyStringKeyPlainObjectWithLoad": collectorMap.put("", "emptyValue"); collectorLoadMap.put("", "loadedValue"); get("") should return "emptyValue" (plain object takes precedence). 

3. "collectorWithNullLoad": collectorMap.put("collectorNullLoad", collectorInstance); collectorLoadMap.put("collectorNullLoad", null); expect collectorInstance.

4. "collectorMapNullValue": collectorMap.put("nullCollector", null); collectorLoadMap.put("nullCollector", "loadedData"); expect null (since object is null, instanceof fails, returns collectorMap.get which is null). 

5. "bothMapsNullValue": collectorMap.put("bothNull", null); collectorLoadMap.put("bothNull", null); expect null.

6. "collectorLoadMapOnlyNullValue": collectorMap missing, collectorLoadMap.put("loadNullOnly", null); expect null (already similar to loadOnly but with null value). Might be redundant.

7. "collectorMapWithNonCollectorAndLoadMapValue": collectorMap.put("plainWithLoad", "plain"); collectorLoadMap.put("plainWithLoad", "loaded"); expect "plain". (covers ignoring load map when not Collector)

8. "collectorMapWithCollectorAndLoadMapValueDifferentType": collectorMap has Collector, load map has a different type (e.g., Integer). Expect that Integer is returned.

We need to ensure not duplicate existing ones. Existing had collectorWithLoad returning "loadedData". That's similar to case 8 but returns loaded string. Our new case could be Integer to show type doesn't matter.

Thus generate JSON with groups maybe separate per scenario or combine under same group "CollectorContext#get - additional". The format expects group name per test function. Could have one group with multiple cases.

We'll produce group "CollectorContext#get - additional cases". Provide cases list.

Make sure to use proper JSON quoting. Values can be strings or numbers; for objects like collectorInstance we can denote as "collectorInstance" placeholder.

We'll need to reference collectorInstance; maybe represent as "collectorInstance" string.

Ok produce JSON.
